title: Operational Reserve & Contract Contingency Policy — Budgeting and Forecasting
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This document defines Redwood Inference’s Operational Reserve and Contract Contingency Policy for budgeting, forecasting, procurement, and revenue recognition touchpoints. The policy establishes standard reserve buckets, triggers, approval flows, accounting treatment guidance, and operational runbooks for when contractual or project uncertainty requires set-aside funding. The intent is to ensure predictable P&L forecasting while preserving the ability to cover contract contingencies and one-off operational risks.

Scope
This policy applies to: 
- All new and renewal customer contracts, purchase orders, and multi-year commitments that result in supplier or customer obligations.
- Capital and operating budget lines that face material delivery, timing, or quality risk.
- Finance, Legal, Procurement, and Product teams owning commitments.
- It does NOT apply to routine, recurring operating expenses below the threshold in the "Thresholds and Reserve Rates" section.

Key Definitions
- Operational Reserve: A short-term budget buffer (cash or committed spend) set aside to cover expected but uncertain operational costs related to deployments, hardware delivery, or one-off vendor remediations.
- Contract Contingency: A contractual risk reserve associated with deliverable-based contracts (e.g., on-prem deployments, customization, professional services) to cover change orders, SLA credits, or remediation costs.
- Forecast Impact Window: The fiscal months during which the reserve is expected to impact the P&L or cash flow.

Policy Principles
1) Predictability: Reserves should make forecast outcomes conservative but not overly pessimistic. Aim for a 70% confidence band when quantifying risk.
2) Transparency: All reserves must be visible on the monthly forecasting pack and tied to a single owner and rationale.
3) Minimum Administrative Overhead: Standardized buckets and thresholds keep approvals lightweight for low-risk items and require wider governance only for high-dollar exposures.
4) Accounting Alignment: Reserve booking guidance aligns to GAAP accounting principles relevant to Redwood (deferred revenue, warranty/obligations, accruals). Finance must be engaged prior to booking.

Thresholds and Reserve Rates (standardized matrix)
- Low risk: single-event exposure < $25,000 -> Operational Reserve: 5% of contract/order value (auto-approve by Procurement lead).
- Medium risk: $25,000 <= exposure < $250,000 -> Operational Reserve: 10% (Finance approval required).
- High risk: exposure >= $250,000 -> Contract Contingency: 12–20% (Finance + Legal + VP approval; contingency percentage calibrated to qualitative risk factors).
- Hardware delivery/long-lead items: add 8% to the computed reserve to reflect logistics risk.
- Multi-year contracts: reserves judged on committed run-rate and ramp schedule; treat first-year obligations as primary for reserve calculation.

Examples
- Example A: 12-month Dedicated capacity commitment, $300,000 annual contract value, delivery includes on-site hardware. Reserve = 300,000 * 12% + 8% hardware add-on = $45,600 + $24,000 = $69,600 (held as contingency until delivery acceptance).
- Example B: One-off professional services PO for $18,000. Reserve = 18,000 * 5% = $900 (auto-approved and reflected in monthly forecast).

Procedure: Requesting a Reserve (step-by-step)
1) Initiator (Product, Customer Success, or Sales) opens a Reserve Request ticket in the Finance Jira project (FIN-RESERVE). Include contract summary, risk drivers, estimated exposure, and expected resolution window.
2) Procurement verifies supplier terms and confirms if an existing PO or escalation path covers the exposure.
3) Finance calculates proposed reserve quantum using the Thresholds matrix and posts a revised forecast line item.
4) Approvals: 
   - Auto-approve if reserve <= $5,000 (Procurement or Finance analyst OK).
   - Finance approval for medium risk (>= $5,000 and < $250,000).
   - Legal + Finance + VP approval for high risk (>= $250,000).
5) Once approved, the reserve is booked as an accrual (see Accounting Treatment) or as a balance sheet reserve in the commitments tracker.

Accounting Treatment Guidance
- Short-term Operational Reserve (expected to be resolved within 12 months): record as an accrued liability (WIP: Contract Contingency Accrual).
- Contract Contingency tied to deferred revenue/milestones: coordinate with RevRec team — if funds are collected but services are incomplete, defer recognition; if exposure results in refunds/credits, record contra-revenue when the obligation is probable and estimable.
- Journal entry examples (illustrative):
  - Booking an accrual for an identified contingency: 
    DR: Contingency Expense (P&L)     $X
    CR: Contingency Accrual (Liability) $X
  - Reversing accrual when contingency not realized: 
    DR: Contingency Accrual (Liability) $X
    CR: Contingency Release (Other income) $X
  - Paying supplier remediation out of accrual: 
    DR: Contingency Accrual (Liability) $X
    CR: Cash / AP                            $X
- All journal entries require Finance reviewer sign-off and must include reference to the Reserve Request ticket ID.

Integration with Budgeting and Forecasting
- Monthly close: active reserves must be included in the rolling 12-month forecast and highlighted in the operating forecast pack.
- Re-forecast cadence: reserves reviewed at each monthly reforecast; if risk narrows, reduce the reserve; if risk increases, submit an amendment request. Changes must be timestamped and rationalized in the forecast notes.
- Scenario sensitivity: include reserve-on and reserve-off scenarios for material deals (> $500k) and surface the incremental impact in the executive forecast deck.

Procurement and Contracting Playbook
1) For any contract, include a standard contingency clause template (Legal will provide language) that defines change order handling and SLA credits.
2) Procurement negotiates a remediation cap where possible and documents supplier warranty or SLA credit mechanisms.
3) If supplier refuses remediation caps for high-risk items, Procurement flags the item and Finance applies the higher contingency rate (up to 20%).
4) Purchase orders that include pass-through third-party hardware should automatically include the hardware delivery buffer (8%) in the procurement estimate.

Revenue Recognition Interactions
- When contingency affects customer deliverables (e.g., deployment not accepted), defer revenue until acceptance criteria are met per RevRec policy.
- If an expected credit is probable (customer claim), recognize a liability and adjust deferred revenue accordingly. Coordinate with the RevRec team to determine whether and how to split performance obligations.
- Documentation: every reserve affecting revenue must include the contract clause, expected remediation path, and the RevRec analyst approval stamp in the Reserve Request ticket.

Governance and Roles
- Finance: calculates reserves, books accruals, maintains commitments tracker, approves medium-risk reserves. Owner: Head of Finance (delegated to Finance Manager).
- Legal: assesses contractual risk, drafts contingency clauses, participates in high-risk approvals. Owner: Senior Counsel, Commercial.
- Procurement: verifies supplier terms, provides remediation history, and negotiates remediation caps. Owner: Procurement Lead.
- Product/CS/Sales: identifies operational risks from customer commitments and files Reserve Requests.

Escalation Matrix
- Day 0–10 after a reserve is opened: Owner works resolution plan and updates FIN-RESERVE ticket weekly.
- Day 10–30: If unresolved and exposure persists, Finance flags in the monthly S&OP meeting and may increase reserve percent.
- >30 days unresolved with material exposure (> $250k): VP Finance + Legal escalate to CEO for decision on contract amendment, credit terms, or cash reserve funding.

Reporting and KPIs
- KPIs to monitor: total contingency outstanding, reserve utilization rate (percent of reserves actually consumed), average time to resolution, number of high-risk reserves > $250k.
- Monthly dashboard: Finance publishes a reserved commitments dashboard (ownership, amount, expected resolution date, utilization history) in the monthly FP&A pack.

Retention and Audit
- All Reserve Request tickets, approval artifacts, and journal entries must be retained for at least 7 years to satisfy audit and compliance needs.
- Quarterly internal audit sample: the Internal Audit team will validate a rotating sample of reserve bookings and supporting evidence.

Appendices
A. Reserve Request template (fields to include):
- Ticket ID, contract/PO number, counterparty, amount at risk, qualitative risk drivers, proposed reserve percentage and computed amount, expected resolution window (dates), supporting documents (contracts, email threads), owner, finance analyst.

B. Sample contingency clause (Legal will provide final wording):
- "In the event of failed acceptance or required remediation related to [scope], Customer and Supplier agree to follow the remediation process documented in Appendix X, and any credits or costs will be calculated per the remedy schedule. Parties will use good faith efforts to resolve issues within 30 days. If resolution is not achieved, Customer may request mediation as described in Section Y."

C. Quick reference — Approvals table:
- <= $5k: Procurement/Finance analyst
- >$5k and < $250k: Finance Manager sign-off
- >= $250k: VP Finance + Legal + Product VP
